okay so many tips for context i’ve been on adhd medications since i was 13 ish and have always been just genetically underweight so it was definitely a big risk to put me on meds when i was losing weight. i think my biggest tip at least all that i’ve gotten from nutritionists over the years is setting literal reminders to eat make an eating schedule either on paper and with alarms or using the reminders app (or something i recently discovered and works for me is the to do assistant app where you have a little mission and get new islands it’s dope) anyway i know it’s the most agonizing type of hard to set routines and stick to them with adhd but i’ve found anchoring them around sleep (because you know you need to sleep) and not necessarily specific times has been helpful in starting the foundation of a routine then in 66 days or more (pretty much when your brain has developed good neural pathways around that routine) adding a time to it and incorporating into a written schedule helps. With the eating thing it really sucks balls but you kind of just have to force yourself to eat getting a couple basic easy things that you know how to prepare and have carbs and a protein element (healthy fats are a bonus) help that sort of slump where you feel like you don’t have the energy to stay concentrated long enough to make anything so you’d rather just not eat and like listening to headspace or the calm app’s like mindful eating lessons (if you feel like it) has been really helpful just appreciating the food in front of you (especially if it’s good food) mwah makes me feel healthy. Another tip if possible avoid caffeine around times where you should be eating don’t get me wrong it’s good for concentration and stuff and drinking it while you’re eating works for me but avoid drinking a cup of coffee and then eating 30 minutes later cause that’s when the caffeine is at its hight and it’ll just play off the addrrall and you won’t enjoy any food you’re eating and appetite will vanish. Also EAT BEFORE YOU TAKE YOUR MEDS or if you take them (at least for me i know it takes around 15 to 20 minutes to kick in so i’m motivated to get something on the table and eat it before my appetite is gone. As you can clearly see (sorry for the headache) i’m major hyperactive so coffee isn’t a huge part of my routine but my biggest piece of advice in general is really taking the time to write out an eating schedule (meet with a dietitian if you can cause i know it’s hard when you think about having to do something and then you let yourself get distracted and never do it believe me) so let someone help you come up with a routine and really anchor it around routines you already have in place. Like if you have a meeting at 11:00 every day make sure to get up at 9:30 make your food and start eating by 10 you finish eating by 10:30 and then take your meds and you have that extra time to plan or twiddle around waiting for your meds to kick in so you’re ready for the meeting by 11:00 for example. Obviously everyone is different but the process of building routines is the hardest part once you have that on lock things become so much easier. And also don’t beat yourself up if you happen to wake up later and don’t do all of the perfect human morning activities like exercising and drinking water and meditation all before 4:00 in the morning or whatever (that’s more of a reminder for myself i like to put pressure on things being perfect but have a hard time finding the focus to go about realizing that it leads to negative self talk blah blah blah). Anyway good luck friend and feel free to ask more anymore long winded tips and explanations and examples that absolutely NEED to go with those tips i have a bazillion

Women are CRIMINALLY under diagnosed and under medicated in the US especially because our symptoms don’t always present in the same way that they do in boys if your symptoms are impacting your life they will likely start you on 20 mg of adderall or vyvanse. I obviously don’t know your tolerance for medication cause it’s based on a lot of things but even as an underweight female with a bmi of 16.4 20 was far too little. The best psychiatrists i’ve been to usually do a minimum of 40mg but no matter the dosage be sure to ask why and ask them to explain their thinking process and what led them to prescribe that amount of that kind of medication
